about: CAL.effs['2x4'] measured on our zone profiles (P0-A): one (2,4) stage, SP=2 TP=4 EP=8, layers 0-6 contiguous (real routing), 1D fabric, bf4 experts, M3_MOE_W_NDSHARD=1 M3_MOE_HYBRID_THRESHOLD=128, v1 dispatch/combine, bf8 index_k cache.
Condition: W=4096 single request at h=139264 (the 141312 request aligned down to whole chunks); prose and code runs pooled. moe = mean of sparse layers 3-6, dense = layer 1.

Formula = sim_core zoneEff: eff = roof / (zone ms - latency floor), clamped to [0.003, 1]. zone ms = MEAN over the 8 chips (Pavlo's statistic, not the worst chip). Floor 0.04 ms for CCL ops, 0.01 ms otherwise; norm_ag = both all-gathers (roof x2, floor x2), as zoneEff's mean-of-two.
Roofline = sim_core roofTok/roofSeg via tools/roofline_ops.js --segments W:139264 --idx bf8 (our index_k cache is bf8; Pavlo's profiles were bf16), imbalance 1.2 in the experts FLOPs, Tr = W.
sparse, indexer, ring_c are multiplied by waveFactor(W)/waveFactor(5120) = 1.0417, so that layerMs at T=W reproduces the measured zone (the sim applies that ratio at run time).

misc = layer zone mean - every mapped op (includes routing_setup, the untracked MoE all-gather and its SP arrival wait). kv_a2a = dispatch. ring_scan 0.015 is Pavlo's placeholder (the pipeline fit replaces it); for 2x4 pipelines the dense ring uses CAL.pipe.ringC, not dense.ring_c.
With opEff = 0 the sim uses min(eff, target): values above target (qkv and experts, at both W) have no effect. Keep CAL.pipe.moeMult (fitted against the same kind of 1D zone profile).
